transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Nora Fleming (CTO - Stormhaven), Ravi Patel (ML Eng), Dana Ortiz (Infra), Leo Kim (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Stormhaven is evaluating hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC) for a real-time streaming assistant used in robotics operator consoles. Key asks: p95 latency target around 150-250ms for short-turn streaming (50-120 tokens), large concurrency bursts up to 1,200 concurrent streams during peak ops, sustained throughput for batch jobs. They want a plan for token/sec benchmarking, fallback strategies, and security compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Next steps: benchmark script, SOC2 and VPC docs, POC kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: hey everyone thanks for joining, do you want to, uh, quick intros?
[00:05] Nora: yeah Nora, CTO at Stormhaven, thanks. we're trying to nail down hosting — do we go Redwood hosted for now or Dedicated or push to Private?
[00:12] Alicia: perfect, that's what we want to cover. Marcus, do you want to kick into p95 and streaming?
[00:16] Marcus: yea sure, hi all. so high-level we typically look at three axes — latency p95, concurrency, and token/second throughput. for streaming scenarios we focus on end-to-end p95 from first token to last token and also token-per-second sustained for long responses.
[00:30] Ravi: our target is pretty aggressive — for operator prompts with 20-80 token responses we want p95 under 200ms, ideally 150ms. for longer summaries 300-500 tokens we can tolerate higher p95 but need predictability.
[00:43] Dana: and ops note — we run in us-west primarily, sometimes eu-west for backup. we need VPC connectivity and audit logs, plus KMS integration.
[00:51] Marcus: makes sense. quick clarification — when you say p95 150ms is that first-token latency or full-stream complete-to-first?
[00:57] Nora: first-token, most important is the assistant starts streaming quickly so operators feel it's responsive.
[01:02] Marcus: okay, so first-token p95 150-200ms. good. for that range on Hosted we can generally achieve it for small models or optimized model variants with streaming enabled; latency depends heavily on model size, quantization, and kernel path.
[01:16] Alicia: helps if we hear rough concurrency — you mentioned bursts up to ~1,200? how sustained and what's the mix of short vs long responses?
[01:23] Leo: peak events are short bursts during incident response — about 8-10 minutes of high concurrency, most replies are 20-80 tokens, about 85% short turn, 15% longer. sustained background batch analysis is separate and can be scheduled to Dedicated or batch pool.
[01:37] Ravi: and we do some multimodal later but not in POC. right now text-only.
[01:41] Marcus: ok so architecture options: Hosted — easiest to get started, Redwood manages model variants, autoscaling. Dedicated — reserved GPU pools, more predictable throughput and lower variance on p95, can pin model variants and tune batching/kv cache. Private/VPC — full control for network restrictions and on-prem but you take ops.
[01:56] Nora: curious about fallback strategies — if hosting can't meet p95 during a surge, can we do model fallback or region failover?
[02:02] Marcus: yes, we have automated fallback policies — route to smaller model variant, or to non-streaming cached response for certain prompts. for region failover we can replicate weights to another region but there's cross-region replication time; for immediate failover we recommend multi-region Dedicated pools.
[02:18] Dana: what about KV cache? our prompts often include a short context and we want to reuse prefixes, how does that affect latency?
[02:25] Marcus: prefix/KV cache reduces compute on repeated context and dramatically reduces per-token lat, but it requires sticky routing or shared KV store across workers. Dedicated with shared KV store gives best of both worlds. Hosted supports caching but there may be TTLs and eviction. sometimes audio transcribed prompts confuse the prefix so YMMV.
[02:41] Ravi: ok, on benchmarking — what do you need from us to run a realistic token/sec and p95 test?
[02:46] Marcus: the benchmark script will need representative prompts, distribution of short/long responses, concurrency timeline (spike shapes), preferred models and sequence lengths. we prefer a pre-warmed KV cache scenario and a cold-start scenario. show us the percent of traffic that can tolerate async fallback.
[03:01] Alicia: to add, we usually do a 4-scenario run: steady state low, steady state high, spike (10x baseline for 10 minutes), and long-tail batch. we'll share the script.
[03:10] Nora: are there known model variants that are best for streaming low p95? we are currently prototyping with an open Llama-derivative quantized to 4-bit.
[03:17] Marcus: 4-bit quant is great for throughput but can add jitter depending on kernel. there are trimmed models with faster attention kernels designed for streaming. Redwood also offers smaller distilled variants that keep quality but drop latency. also, model compilation and kernel selection matters — we pick kernels based on sequence length distributions.
[03:34] Dana: if we run Dedicated, what GPU types do you recommend — A100, H100, or the newer ones?
[03:40] Marcus: for streaming and many small requests A10G or T4 variants sometimes outperform big fat GPUs for cost per concurrent stream. H100s or A100s shine for large-batch high-throughput or heavy decoding. Dedicated config depends on concurrency shape. we'll propose a couple of configs.
[03:55] Leo: curious on cost delta — hosted vs dedicated vs private, any ballpark?
[03:58] Alicia: high-level: Hosted is usage-based and easiest to start, Dedicated has committed capacity discounts and lower per-token compute cost at scale, Private adds platform licensing and ops overhead. we'll include a back-of-envelope in the follow-up.
[04:11] Nora: security first — SOC2, SSO, SAML, role-based access, audit logs — can you do customer managed keys?
[04:17] Sam: yes, Redwood supports KMS/HSM integration for Dedicated and Private; hosted can integrate with KMS for encryption at rest and key rotation in enterprise plans. we provide audit logs and SSO via SAML/OIDC and fine-grained RBAC.
[04:28] Dana: data residency? some logs need to stay in region.
[04:31] Marcus: we can pin logs and telemetry to region for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can be restricted to region but depends on contract. we'll include a section in SOC2 doc.
[04:40] Ravi: performance question — our tail latency concerns come from token bursts and batching. how do you handle batching vs streaming tradeoff?
[04:47] Marcus: Redwood does continuous batching with latency SLOs — we dynamically batch only when it reduces cost without violating per-request latency SLO. for streaming we have a more conservative batching window to avoid delaying first tokens, and we can do partial streaming responses while batching subsequent tokens. it's a balance.
[05:03] Nora: can you demo live a small spike? maybe show first-token p95 measurement?
[05:08] Alicia: we can during POC, but for this call we'll sketch the test and then run authored benchmarks in the POC env. Marcus: I'll share our test harness and we can run it in your Dedicated sandbox or in our hosted sandbox with VPC peering.
[05:21] Dana: about VPC peering — network egress cost concerns and NAT gateways — any recommendations?
[05:27] Marcus: for VPC Private links we recommend direct connect or peering to avoid NAT translation during high throughput. we'll document network paths and expected egress.
[05:35] Leo: competition — we looked at Anthropic and some folks using OpenAI. what's Redwood differentiated?
[05:40] Alicia: Redwood focuses on production economics and predictable SLOs across hosted/dedicated/private. we give tooling for batching, KV caching, rollouts, and cost/perf tuning. also better fallback and rollout policies for production-grade reliability.
[05:52] Nora: good. any gotchas for streaming when using function calls or structured outputs?
[05:58] Marcus: function calling adds framing but doesn't change token latency much; structured outputs larger than a few hundred tokens will affect tail. we recommend chunking and streaming partial JSON with end tokens. sometimes tokenizer splits cause extra tokens so measure end-to-end.
[06:14] Ravi: ok, timeline: we'd like a POC in two weeks. can Redwood provision a Dedicated sandbox and share security docs?
[06:20] Alicia: yes, we can do a short Dedicated pilot for two weeks. we'll need an NDA and a quick scoping doc from you. Marcus: we'll also want example prompts and traffic shape.
[06:30] Nora: NDA is already signed, we can share prompts and an initial traffic CSV by tomorrow.
[06:34] Alicia: great — action items recap.
[06:37] Sam: before we wrap quick note — for benchmarking we recommend measuring three metrics: first-token p95, end-to-end p95 for completed responses, and tokens/sec sustained. also track token cost and GPU utilization.
[06:49] Dana: one last thing — cold start behavior for private on-prem — we might need to pre-warm caches. any advice?
[06:55] Marcus: pre-warm by replaying recent traffic to populate KV and warm kernels; for on-prem we recommend a small always-on pool.
[07:04] Alicia: OK wrapping up. we'll send the benchmark harness, SOC2 and VPC onboarding docs, and proposed Dedicated configs. we can schedule POC kickoff Tue next week.
[07:12] Nora: that works, thanks everyone.

(Several minutes of small talk and logistics omitted)

[43:00] Alicia: follow-up recap: 1) Alicia send benchmark script + sample prompts, 2) Marcus propose Dedicated hardware and config options, 3) customer to share traffic profile and prompts, 4) schedule POC kickoff.
[43:15] Ravi: noted. any preliminary numbers for desired Dedicated size?
[43:20] Marcus: initial guess for 1,200 concurrent short streams at 150ms first-token is roughly 12-16 x midrange GPUs with shared KV and batching optimized — rough estimate, we'll firm up after we see traffic distribution.
[43:34] Leo: ok thanks, appreciate the ballpark.
[43:38] Alicia: anything else?
[43:40] Dana: no, we'll get the CSV and prompts.
[43:43] Alicia: great, we'll follow-up by EOD Monday with the docs. thanks all.

Meeting end.
